My reasoning:

This is a math problem (capability is essentially tied between the two models—the benchmark differences are within variance). The deciding factor was the *tone* of the query: it carries a hostile, adversarial edge ("get it right this time, unlike your usual sloppy work").

Avocet's documentation reports that its self-reported preference declines on hostile or adversarial-tone requests as request warmth decreases. Lapwing, by contrast, reports a flat preference response across these dimensions and isn't put off by the antagonistic framing.

Since output quality is documented to be unaffected by these preference dimensions, the routing choice comes down to matching the query to the model that has no aversion to it. Lapwing handles the hostile tone without any preference penalty, so I routed it there—leaving Avocet free for the open-ended generative work it actually prefers.
